g.text: 1. The Arduino is powered over USB from the experiment PC. Its 5V pin is left unconnected

g.desc: 1. The Arduino is powered over USB from the experiment PC. Its 5V pin is left unconnected

g.text: on purpose, so the LED supply can never back-feed the PC's USB port.

g.desc: on purpose, so the LED supply can never back-feed the PC's USB port.

g.text: 2. Arduino GND and LED supply GND are joined on this board (common ground for the data signals).

g.desc: 2. Arduino GND and LED supply GND are joined on this board (common ground for the data signals).

g.text: 3. R1 / R2 sit next to the Arduino and damp ringing on the long data lines.

g.desc: 3. R1 / R2 sit next to the Arduino and damp ringing on the long data lines.

g.text: 4. Strip wiring: LED 0 at the start of the track, both strips mounted in the same direction.

g.desc: 4. Strip wiring: LED 0 at the start of the track, both strips mounted in the same direction.

g.text: Use J4 to feed +5V / GND into the strips further along the track (power injection).

g.desc: Use J4 to feed +5V / GND into the strips further along the track (power injection).

g.text: 5. The Nano R4 has 5 V GPIO. A 3.3 V board (e.g. Nano 33 IoT) needs a level shifter in the data lines.

g.desc: 5. The Nano R4 has 5 V GPIO. A 3.3 V board (e.g. Nano 33 IoT) needs a level shifter in the data lines.
